hints: Focus on what sodium propanoate actually is, the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid with three carbons.
Check mixture 1 first, NaBH4 is a reducing agent that turns the aldehyde CH3CH2CHO into propan-1-ol, not a carboxylate.
Compare making an alkoxide with Na metal versus making a carboxylate by alkaline hydrolysis, then see which mixture really gives the COO- group.
walkthrough:
**Recall the target product**

Sodium propanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$. It contains a carboxylate group.

To make it you need oxidation to a carboxylic acid level or hydrolysis that creates a $\text{COO}^-$ group.

**Test mixture 1**

$\text{NaBH}_4$ is a reducing agent. It donates hydride to reduce aldehydes to primary alcohols.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

This is propan-1-ol, not sodium propanoate. So 1 is out.

**Test mixture 2**

An alcohol plus sodium metal gives a sodium alkoxide plus hydrogen, an acid-base type reaction, not oxidation.

$$2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{O}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{H}_2$$

The product is sodium propoxide. Notice the name is very similar but chemically different from sodium propanoate. So 2 is out.

**Test mixture 3**

Nitriles are hydrolysed by heating under reflux with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ to give the sodium carboxylate plus ammonia.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{NaOH(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{NH}_3$$

Here the two-carbon chain plus the nitrile carbon gives the three-carbon propanoate. So only 3 works.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes 1 and 2. Mixture 1 gives propan-1-ol by reduction, and mixture 2 gives sodium propoxide plus hydrogen, neither contains the carboxylate group needed for sodium propanoate.
options.B: Incorrect because both 1 and 2 are wrong. Students often think NaBH4 oxidises or that Na with an alcohol oxidises it to a salt of the acid, but NaBH4 reduces and Na only replaces the OH hydrogen to form an alkoxide.
options.C: Incorrect because although 3 is correct, 2 is not. The trap is confusing sodium propoxide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{ONa}$) with sodium propanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa}$). Only the second has a C=O in a COO- group.
options.D: Correct because only mixture 3 gives sodium propanoate. Alkaline hydrolysis of propanenitrile under reflux produces $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$ plus $\text{NH}_3$, while 1 gives an alcohol and 2 gives an alkoxide.
